meta_description: Collections rebuilt around governed agents — right-party contact up 21% and promise-to-pay rate up 18% at the same staffing

blocks.x: Collections rebuilt around governed agents — right-party contact up 21% and promise-to-pay rate up 18% at the same staffing

a US consumer-finance lender whose collections floor had become a dialer factory: agents touched accounts in list order, not in order of recoverable value. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
The baseline fortnight counted what the list-order design cost: 11% right-party contact, and the accounts most likely to cure were reached last because they looked like everyone else in the queue.
Compliance lived in a laminated card at each desk. Call scripts drifted from it within weeks of every policy update, and nobody could prove which version a specific call had used.

We moved collections to governed agents: each account ranked by recoverable value and channel preference, outreach sequenced SMS-voice-email within state rules, and every conversation ran on the current script version with the compliance state machine enforcing it. Agents handle what the machine cannot settle; the envelope is fixed, and nothing outside it ships.

blocks.x: The transferable assets are the compliance state machine and the value-ranked queue design. Both have run elsewhere with new rulepacks. The propensity models do not travel; they are trained on each book's own behavior, which is exactly why the diagnostic comes first.
Figures on this page are the client's, reproduced with permission. Method notes and measurement designs are available under NDA.
Start with the diagnostic, not the contract: the same diagnostic that baselined this program takes two weeks, and a scoped proposal follows only if the delta justifies it.
